UI Wireframes

Low-fidelity screen sketches for the AB-Verified curated IT marketplace. These describe structure, content and available actions, not visual design. Every screen is server-rendered HTML with htmx-driven partial updates; no client-side framework is implied by any layout here. There are exactly three personas: Client, Contractor and Staff. Requirement identifiers refer to ../SPEC.md. Colour, type and the square-cornered geometry follow ../palette/: Roboto throughout, Kinetic navy as ink, Kinetic red as the accent, and no rounded corners anywhere.

Grey box = container Hatched box = deferred / placeholder content 1 = numbered annotation below the screen Amber block = behavioural rule, not visible chrome Green bar = demo-mode chrome, non-production only

IT work, between verified Australian businesses.

Clients post work. Our team verifies every business against the Australian Business Register, approves each job, and invites the contractors best suited to it. No open job board, no bid spam.

Screen content (S-04, S-07, S-10 and so on) unchanged
  1. No privileged code path. Demo sign-in performs an ordinary password authentication against a seeded account and receives an ordinary session (FR-153). It never uses the service role key, so a demo session cannot see more than the persona it represents.
  2. Absent, not disabled, in production. With DEMO_MODE=false the cards are not rendered and POST /demo/login returns 404, so a stale bookmark reaches nothing (FR-152, FR-158).
  3. The outbox holds the email and SMS a demo run would have sent (FR-157), so a tester can read the invitation without a message reaching a real person.
